blocked.reason: Condensed milk is already sweet, so it can’t be Kosong. For no sugar, choose O or C.

name: Kopi

steps.text: Put the kopi powder in the sock, hold it over a jug and pour the boiling water through it slowly. Let it drip through.
Spoon the condensed milk into a cup or jug.
Spoon the evaporated milk into a cup or jug.
Add the sugar.
Pour the kopi into the cup and stir.
Top up with the hot water and stir.
Stir the kopi in the jug, then fill a glass with the ice and pour it over.
Top up with the cold water and stir.

tools.name: Kopi sock
tools.alternative: a fine sieve lined with a paper towel, or a kopi bag steeped like a tea bag

tools.name: Small jug
tools.alternative: a large mug

about: Kopitiam coffee is brewed strong through a cloth sock, then softened with sweet condensed milk. The beans are mostly robusta roasted dark with a little sugar and margarine, so the cup is bold and smoky and stands up to the milk.

blocked.reason: Condensed milk is already sweet, so it can’t be Kosong. For no sugar, choose O or C.

name: Yuan Yang

steps.text: Put the kopi powder and tea dust in the sock, hold it over a jug and pour the boiling water through them slowly.
Spoon the condensed milk into a cup or jug.
Spoon the evaporated milk into a cup or jug.
Add the sugar.
Pour the yuan yang into the cup and stir.
Top up with the hot water and stir.
Stir the yuan yang in the jug, then fill a glass with the ice and pour it over.
Top up with the cold water and stir.

tools.name: Kopi sock
tools.alternative: a fine sieve lined with a paper towel, or a kopi bag steeped like a tea bag

tools.name: Small jug
tools.alternative: a large mug

about: Coffee and tea in one cup, named after a pair of mandarin ducks that are always seen together. The tea softens the coffee’s bitterness and the coffee gives the tea more body.

blocked.reason: Condensed milk is already sweet, so it can’t be Kosong. For no sugar, choose O or C.

name: Teh

steps.text: Put the tea dust in the sock and pour the boiling water through it into a jug. Let it stand for 3 minutes, then lift the sock out.
Spoon the condensed milk into a cup or jug.
Spoon the evaporated milk into a cup or jug.
Add the sugar.
Pour the teh into the cup and stir.
Top up with the hot water and stir.
Stir the teh in the jug, then fill a glass with the ice and pour it over.
Top up with the cold water and stir.

tools.name: Kopi sock
tools.alternative: a fine sieve lined with a paper towel, or a kopi bag steeped like a tea bag

tools.name: Small jug
tools.alternative: a large mug

about: Strong black tea brewed through a sock, made creamy and sweet with condensed milk. Brewing it dark means the tea still tastes like tea once the milk goes in.

name: Teh Tarik

steps.text: Put the tea dust in the sock and pour the boiling water through it into a mug. Let it stand for 3 minutes, then lift the sock out.
Stir in the condensed milk and evaporated milk.
Stir in the water.
Pull the tea: pour it from one mug into the other from a little height, back and forth five or six times, until a froth forms on top.
Pour it over a glass of ice.

tools.name: Two mugs with handles
tools.alternative: a jug and a mug

tools.name: Kopi sock
tools.alternative: a tea bag or a fine sieve

about: Teh tarik is pulled: poured back and forth between two mugs until it is frothy on top and cool enough to drink. The pulling mixes the milk right through and gives it a smooth, light feel.

blocked.reason: Condensed milk is already sweet, so it can’t be Kosong. For no sugar, choose O or C.

name: Teh Halia

steps.text: Slice the ginger thinly.
Simmer the ginger in the boiling water for 5 minutes, then pour it through the tea dust in the sock into a jug.
Spoon the condensed milk into a cup or jug.
Spoon the evaporated milk into a cup or jug.
Add the sugar.
Pour the teh halia into the cup and stir.
Top up with the hot water and stir.
Stir the teh halia in the jug, then fill a glass with the ice and pour it over.
Top up with the cold water and stir.

tools.name: Small saucepan
tools.alternative: a mug of ginger slices topped up from the kettle and left for 10 minutes

tools.name: Kopi sock
tools.alternative: a fine sieve lined with a paper towel, or a kopi bag steeped like a tea bag

about: Teh with fresh ginger simmered into it. Halia is the Malay word for ginger. It is warming and a little peppery, a favourite on rainy days.

blocked.reason: Milo with milk is made with condensed milk, which is already sweet. For no added sugar, choose O.

name: Milo

steps.text: Stir the Milo powder into the boiling water until smooth.
Stir in the condensed milk.
Stir in the sugar.
Top up with the hot water and stir.
Fill a glass with the ice and pour in the Milo.
Top up with the cold water and stir.

tools.name: Teaspoon
tools.alternative: any spoon

about: Malted chocolate stirred into hot water and sweetened with condensed milk. Gau means more Milo for a thicker cup. Its small amount of caffeine comes from the cocoa.

name: Milo Dinosaur

ingredients.note: two-thirds to stir in, the rest to heap on top

steps.text: Stir two-thirds of the Milo powder into the boiling water until smooth.
Stir in the condensed milk.
Fill a glass with the ice, pour in the Milo and top up with the cold water.
Heap the rest of the Milo powder on top and serve with a spoon.

tools.name: Tall glass
tools.alternative: any large glass

about: Iced Milo with a mound of dry Milo powder on top, eaten with a spoon as it slowly sinks. A Singapore and Malaysia invention, named for being bigger than the usual.

blocked.reason: Horlicks with milk is made with condensed milk, which is already sweet. For no added sugar, choose O.

name: Horlicks

steps.text: Stir the Horlicks powder into the boiling water until smooth.
Stir in the condensed milk.
Stir in the sugar.
Top up with the hot water and stir.
Fill a glass with the ice and pour in the Horlicks.
Top up with the cold water and stir.

tools.name: Teaspoon
tools.alternative: any spoon

about: Malted milk, sweet and biscuity, with no chocolate and no caffeine. A gentle drink for any time of day, and a good one for children.

name: Barley

steps.text: Rinse the pearl barley, then simmer it in the boiling water for 45 minutes until soft. Strain, keeping the water.
Stir in the sugar while it is still warm.
Stir in the water and pour it into a cup.
Let it cool, then stir in the cold water.
Pour it over a glass of ice.

tools.name: Saucepan with a lid
tools.alternative: a rice cooker on its porridge setting

about: Pearl barley simmered in water gives a pale, gently nutty drink. It is usually served cold and lightly sweet, and many people drink it to cool down on a hot day.

name: Water Chestnut

steps.text: Peel the water chestnuts and chop them roughly. Tinned ones only need chopping.
Simmer the chopped water chestnuts in the boiling water for 20 minutes, then strain out the pieces, or keep a few to eat.
Stir in the sugar until it dissolves.
Stir in the water and pour it into a cup.
Let it cool, then stir in the cold water.
Pour it over a glass of ice.

tools.name: Saucepan
tools.alternative: a large microwave-safe bowl, covered

tools.name: Sieve
tools.alternative: a slotted spoon

about: Water chestnuts simmered and lightly sweetened make a clear, delicate drink with a faint natural sweetness. It is one of the classic cooling drinks of the drinks stall.

name: Chrysanthemum

steps.text: Put the dried flowers in a teapot and pour the boiling water over them. Leave for 5 minutes, then strain.
Stir in the sugar.
Stir in the water and pour it into a cup.
Let it cool, then stir in the cold water.
Pour it over a glass of ice.

tools.name: Teapot
tools.alternative: a mug with a saucer on top

tools.name: Tea strainer
tools.alternative: a small sieve

about: A golden, floral tea of dried chrysanthemum flowers, with no caffeine at all. Lightly sweetened, it is soothing hot and refreshing iced.

name: Lime Juice

steps.text: Cut the calamansi in half.
Squeeze the juice into a jug through a small sieve to catch the seeds.
Stir in the sugar until it dissolves.
Stir in the cold water.
Pour it over a glass of ice.

tools.name: Small sieve
tools.alternative: pick out the seeds with a teaspoon

about: Calamansi, the small fragrant limes of the region, squeezed and sweetened into a sharp, refreshing drink. Always served cold.

name: Bandung

steps.text: Stir the rose syrup and evaporated milk together until the colour is an even pink.
Top up with the hot water and stir.
Add the ice.
Top up with the cold water and stir.

tools.name: Long spoon
tools.alternative: a chopstick

about: The pink rose milk found at drink stalls across Singapore. Rose syrup is very sweet and floral, and evaporated milk gives it body without the heaviness of cream.

name: Soya Bean Milk

steps.text: Tie the pandan leaf into a knot, if you have one.
Warm the soy milk with the pandan leaf in a small pot until it just begins to steam. Do not let it boil.
Stir the pandan leaf through the soy milk and leave it in the fridge for 10 minutes.
Take out the pandan leaf, if you used one.
Stir in the sugar.
Stir in the water.
Pour it over a glass of ice.

tools.name: Small pot
tools.alternative: a mug in the microwave, in short bursts

about: Smooth soy milk, lightly sweetened and scented with pandan, the way the soya bean stall serves it. It contains soy, and no dairy.

name: Long Black

steps.text: Pour the hot water into the cup.
Make a double espresso straight on top, so the crema stays.

tools.name: Espresso machine
tools.alternative: a moka pot, or 2 tsp strong instant coffee in 60 ml just-boiled water

about: A double espresso poured over hot water. Putting the water in first keeps the crema, the golden foam, on top, so it tastes rounder than coffee topped up the other way.

name: Latte
meaning: Espresso with plenty of steamed milk

steps.text: Make a double espresso into the cup.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, with a thin layer of foam.
Pour the milk into the espresso, finishing with a little foam on top.

tools.name: Espresso machine
tools.alternative: a moka pot, or 2 tsp strong instant coffee in 60 ml just-boiled water

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: Espresso with lots of steamed milk and a thin cap of foam. The milk softens the coffee, so it is the gentlest of the espresso drinks.

name: Cappuccino
meaning: Espresso with milk and thick foam

steps.text: Make a double espresso into the cup.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, letting in plenty of air for a thick foam.
Pour in the milk, then spoon the foam on top.

tools.name: Espresso machine
tools.alternative: a moka pot, or 2 tsp strong instant coffee in 60 ml just-boiled water

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: Espresso, steamed milk and a deep layer of foam in roughly equal parts. The foam makes it feel light and keeps it warm.

name: Flat White

steps.text: Make a double espresso into the cup.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, with only a little air, so it stays silky.
Pour the milk in steadily, finishing with a heart if you can.

tools.name: Espresso machine
tools.alternative: a moka pot, or 2 tsp strong instant coffee in 60 ml just-boiled water

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: A double espresso with a little velvety milk, so the coffee leads. The milk is thin and silky rather than foamy.

name: Mocha

steps.text: Make a double espresso into a mug.
Stir in the cocoa powder and sugar until smooth.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, with a little foam.
Pour the milk in and stir once.

tools.name: Espresso machine
tools.alternative: a moka pot, or 2 tsp strong instant coffee in 60 ml just-boiled water

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: A latte with chocolate stirred through the espresso. The cocoa adds a little more caffeine of its own.

name: Iced Latte
meaning: Espresso over cold milk and ice

steps.text: Fill a tall glass with the ice and pour in the cold milk.
Make a double espresso and pour it slowly over the milk, so it settles in layers.

tools.name: Espresso machine
tools.alternative: a moka pot, or 2 tsp strong instant coffee in 60 ml just-boiled water

about: Espresso poured over cold milk and ice, so it drifts down in layers. Stir before drinking, or enjoy watching it mix.

name: Babyccino

steps.text: Froth the milk until warm, not hot, then pour it into the cup with the foam on top.

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: Warm frothed milk in a café cup, with no coffee at all. A treat for children that looks like the grown-ups’ drink.

name: Matcha Latte
meaning: Whisked green tea with steamed milk

ingredients.note: left to cool for a minute

steps.text: Sift the matcha into a bowl and add the hot water, left to cool for a minute after boiling.
Whisk briskly until smooth and frothy, then stir in the sugar.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, with a little foam.
Pour the milk into a mug and pour the matcha in on top.

tools.name: Matcha whisk
tools.alternative: a small whisk or a fork, in a wide cup so nothing splashes

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: Matcha whisked smooth and topped with steamed milk. Water just off the boil keeps it from tasting bitter.

name: Iced Matcha Latte
meaning: Whisked green tea over cold milk

steps.text: Whisk the matcha and sugar with the water until smooth, with no lumps.
Fill a tall glass with the ice and pour in the cold milk.
Pour the matcha over the top.

tools.name: Matcha whisk
tools.alternative: shake it with the cold water in a small closed jar

about: Bright green matcha floating on cold milk and ice. No hot water needed, so it is quick to make.

name: Hojicha Latte
meaning: Roasted green tea with steamed milk

steps.text: Whisk the hojicha powder with the boiling water until smooth.
Stir in the sugar.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, with a little foam.
Pour the milk in over the tea.

tools.name: Matcha whisk
tools.alternative: a small whisk or a fork, in a wide cup so nothing splashes

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: Roasted green tea whisked into warm milk. Toasty and gentle, with far less caffeine than coffee.

name: Chai Latte

steps.text: Steep the tea bag and chai spice in the boiling water for 4 minutes.
Lift out the tea bag and stir in the sugar.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, with a little foam.
Pour the milk in over the spiced tea.

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: Black tea brewed with warm spices, then made creamy with milk. Sweet, fragrant and gently warming.

name: London Fog
meaning: Earl Grey with vanilla and steamed milk

steps.text: Steep the Earl Grey in the boiling water for 4 minutes, then lift it out.
Stir in the vanilla syrup.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, with plenty of foam.
Pour the milk into the tea, spooning the foam on top.

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: Earl Grey tea with vanilla and frothy milk, soft and grey like its name. The bergamot in the tea smells of orange peel.

name: Iced Lemon Tea
meaning: Sweet black tea with lemon, over ice

steps.text: Steep the tea bag in the boiling water for 3 minutes, then lift it out.
Stir in the sugar until it dissolves.
Cut two thin slices from the lemon, then squeeze the juice from the rest into the tea.
Fill a tall glass with the ice and lemon slices, pour in the tea and top up with the cold water.

tools.name: Citrus squeezer
tools.alternative: press the lemon with a fork as you squeeze

about: Black tea sweetened while hot, sharpened with lemon and poured over ice. Cooling the tea with cold water keeps it from going cloudy.

name: Rooibos Latte
meaning: Red herbal tea with steamed milk

steps.text: Steep the rooibos in the boiling water for 5 minutes, then lift it out.
Stir in the sugar.
Steam the milk until hot and glossy, with a little foam.
Pour the milk in over the tea.

tools.name: Milk frother or steam wand
tools.alternative: shake cold milk in a closed jar until foamy, then take the lid off and warm it in the microwave in short bursts

about: A red herbal tea with steamed milk: naturally sweet, a little nutty, and with no caffeine at all, so it suits any time of day.
